# Shipment Preparation Functions

Reusable functions for preparing, receiving and tracking shipping-instruction documents under a configured clause. This type adds shipment-specific checks to the inherited preparation and admission workflow. Preparation, selection and readiness describe document processing; they do not confirm shipment execution or delivery.

## Shipment-specific rules

- `domainPrepare(prepared)` requires the prepared document to match the required shipping-instruction template type, otherwise rejecting with `SHIPPING_INSTRUCTION_TEMPLATE_REQUIRED`. Its `/clauses/activation/parameters/parties` must contain a `carrier` key, otherwise `SHIPMENT_CARRIER_REQUIRED`. This guard checks key presence.
- The hook returns the prepared document’s `/shipmentTerms`, using `{}` when absent. The preparation entry stores this object as `domainTerms`.
- `domainValidateCandidate(candidate, frozenTerms)` requires the candidate’s `/shipmentTerms`, also read as `{}` when absent, to equal `frozenTerms`; differences cause `SHIPMENT_TERMS_MISMATCH`. Allowed specialization does not waive this comparison.
- `domainNextActions(documentRef)` always returns `[]`. This supplies no shipment-specific next-action descriptions and makes no claim that shipping work is complete.

The inherited wrappers require these hooks to leave document changes and events untouched and return an object, boolean and list respectively.

## Configuration and preparation

`preparePublic(input)` uses the configured template and requires a nonempty `bindings.parties` mapping. `key` defaults to `single` and must be nonempty text; a clause whose `cardinality` is `single` permits only that key. `prepareKeyedPublic` requires an explicit nonempty `key`. `requestId` defaults to `key` and must also be nonempty text. `fields` and `values` default to `{}` and form part of the preparation intent alongside the configuration and template identities.

The clause type’s `destinationBinding` identifies the destination in `bindings`. A singleton uses that destination directly; collection entries use a JSON-pointer-escaped key beneath it. A new preparation rejects an occupied destination. An existing entry must have the same recorded intent, otherwise `PREPARATION_OBLIGATION_CONFLICT`.

Configuration changes how the document is obtained:

- `obtain` defaults to `create`; only `create` and `provide` are accepted. `create` writes the prepared document to the destination and records `selected` with `documentOrigin`. It rejects nonempty `suppliedParties`.
- `provide` records `awaiting_provider` and requires nonempty `suppliedBy`, stored as `supplier`. It emits `Document Provision Requested` identifying the supplier, `inResponseTo` request and exact `requirementRef`.
- `suppliedParties` defaults to `[]` and identifies party roles to be supplied during provision. `specialization/dataPaths` defaults to `[]`; configured paths must identify existing data declarations, avoid reserved execution and identity areas, and neither duplicate nor overlap another slot.

Preparation emits `Document Prepared` with `clauseId`, `itemKey`, `requestId`, `requirementRef` and `status`. A provision request records requested work, not receipt of a qualifying document.

## Provision and document state

`providePublic` takes an initialized `document`, `inResponseTo`, `requirementRef` and an entry `key`, which defaults to `single`. The entry must expect `provide`, `call/channel` must equal its `supplier`, and both request references must match. Provision rejects entries in `reapproval_required`, `admission_denied`, `cancelled` or `cancellation_requested`.

Validation compares the candidate’s initialized source and effective clause policy against the prepared requirement after permitted normalization. Declared slots must be filled and satisfy their constraints. Supplied data must remain unchanged between the initialized source and current candidate; party identities must remain consistent, undeclared parties are rejected, and `/activation/required` must match the prepared approval policy. Provision reads missing stored `prepareFor` as `inherited`; `bootstrap` invokes additional bootstrap-party and access checks. A staged or selected process identity cannot be replaced by another origin.

Entries live under `/process_<clauseKey>/entries`, indexed by the identity of `key`. Each records its `itemPath`, destination `path`, prepared requirement, frozen `domainTerms`, request references and progress. These paths belong to the document executing the functions. Paths inspected inside `prepared`, `candidate` or a selected instruction belong to that instruction.

A validated candidate may remain `admission_pending`, `awaiting_activation` or `linking`. Once staged as `ready`, provision writes its reference to the destination, records `selected` and emits `Document Selected`. An accepted provision call can therefore record intermediate progress without selecting a document.

When `sharedRefresh` runs, it checks an initialized selected document’s origin against `documentOrigin`. It records `usable` only when that document is active and its named sources are ready; otherwise it records `selected`. Source readiness checks initialization, declared origin, activation and party coverage, including matching lead channels and reader keys. A configured source `selectionPath` must also identify this instruction’s process. Transition to `usable` emits `Document Attached`; later loss of readiness can return the entry to `selected`. Missing state does not establish completion or failure.

## Admission and cancellation

When `bindings.sources` includes `self`, candidate parties not covered by the host roster require admission and configured `/clauses/activation/parameters/admission/approvers`. Admission records the candidate, missing parties, access documents and host activation revision. Installation requires a matching approved grant, approval from every entering party, the same activation revision and valid access. An access request alone does not confirm access. `finishAdmission` requires `installing` and verified host roster coverage, then records `linking` and an `admitted` event status.

A decline causes `admission_denied`; a changed host activation revision requires reapproval. `rebaseAdmissionPublic` requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be `true`, an approver channel, the current `admissionRef` and `reapproval_required`. It clears the admission token and consents, increments `admissionAttempt` and returns the entry to `awaiting_provider` for reprovision.

`cancelPublic` uses `key`, defaulting to `single`. It requires an existing entry without `documentOrigin`, records `cancellation_requested` and emits a request correlated to the preparation. Repeating that request returns `duplicate`. This does not confirm cancellation; a selected process requires domain cancellation. Callable functions alone establish no personal obligation or viewer permission.
